newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Dec electricity expires up in late rebound.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Dec electricity expires up in late rebound.

text.p: NYMEX December electricity expired higher Friday in a late rebound, erasing earlier losses amid strength in the natural gas market.
"We did see some good consolidation late today," said a New York-based broker.
Some brokers and traders said the considerable December open interest that needed to be closed out before expiration also ignited the market's late push upward.
January 1997 Henry Hub natgas futures settled at $3.437 per million British thermal units, up 13.3 cents from Thursday's close.
But December natural gas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub finished near $3.45, down from Thursday's $3.59 after talked as high as $3.75 today.
The electricity futures complex were pressured lower for most of the day amid easing cash prices and outlook of weather in the Pacific Northwest moderating from recent lows.
December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures expired up 76 cents at $28.76 after traded between $27.00 and $29.40.
January 1997 COB settled down 15 cents at $24.48 after hitting a low of $23.50. Deferred COB ended 15 to 65 cents lower.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures expired up 67 cents at $28.58 after swinging between $26.75 and $29.50.
January 1997 PV settled down 45 cents at $23.55, trimming a 95 cent loss. Most outer PV months ended 15 to 67 lowers.
Despite Thursday's loss, December COB still gained $3.26 or 12.8 percent from a week ago, and December PV rose $4.99 or 17.4 percent.
After a volatile, record-setting week, brokers and marketers were mixed in their outlook for the complex.
"The direction is really uncertain, but it could find support at current levels," said a trader in Houston.
"January will take a turn downward," said another Houston trader.

She noted Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will have ample power to offer coming weeks when hydroelectric dam flow restrictions in the Northwest related to fish spawning are scheduled at the end of November.
NYMEX estimated 348 COB and 154 PV contracts were sold.
